what_this_is: The proof targets the factory throughput redesign must meet. Every row is a TARGET, stored here so a later order can measure against it; none is claimed. A row's status moves to ACHIEVED only by a committed measurement artifact that names the run, the market and the instrument, never by editing this file.

unit_conventions.minutes: wall-clock minutes of the named interval, measured by the instrument named in the row
unit_conventions.count: an integer count over the named population

targets.population: a LARGE new market (Nashville-sized: >= 150 census identities)
targets.interval: first acquisition action -> SOURCE_READY (shadow market PROMOTION_READY = YES with 0 blockers)
targets.current_evidence: Nashville 001: 125 active minutes to PROMOTION_READY over 181 census (launch_packages/pettripfinder/markets/reports/nashville_tn_speed_benchmark_004.json on worker/ptf-nashville-new-market-001); Chattanooga 001: ~300 active minutes over 102 census (chattanooga_tn_factory_speed_001.json). Neither is SOURCE_READY in the release sense: neither was promoted.
targets.instrument: the market's speed benchmark report plus the throughput_profile plugin over the validation lanes it runs

targets.population: one market admitted to the serialized release lane
targets.interval: lane admission (promotion order starts) -> targeted live verification complete
targets.current_evidence: Toledo promotion 002 + launch 003 ran FOUR broad regressions (toledo_full 7476 s, toledo_full2 6293 s, toledo_full3 6743 s, toledo_launch 5714 s) inside the lane: 437 minutes of regression alone, measured from the junit files (atlas_throughput_001_broad_run_profiles.json).
targets.instrument: throughput_profile plugin session rows for every validation the lane runs; deployment record timestamps for deploy and live verification

targets.population: two other market workers active while release work runs
targets.unit: count of other workers whose acquisition lanes complete at their solo rate within a stated tolerance
targets.current_evidence: Not measurable today: a broad run peaks at 7.6 GB working set and drove system free memory to 46 MB on a 16 GB box (atlas_throughput_001_sampler_cha_full.json). Chattanooga's own report records its OSM index build at ~70 minutes 'while another market's full broad regression held the CPU'.
targets.instrument: process sampler CSV over the release lane plus each worker's speed benchmark

targets.interval: founder decisions: packet review, rulings, launch decision, deploy authorization
targets.current_evidence: UNKNOWN. No committed artifact timestamps founder active time; founder packets record item counts (Nashville 25 items, Chattanooga 26) but not minutes.
targets.instrument: founder packet open/close timestamps recorded by the review tool (to be added by a later order)

targets.population: an ordinary proven data-only market change (shadow market, no shared module, no authority of another market)
targets.current_evidence: Nashville 001 ran 0 broad regressions during acquisition BY CHOICE, but the classifier would have demanded one: regression_delta classifies its 45 changed paths as GENERIC_RUNTIME_CHANGE x18, ROUTING_SEMANTIC_CHANGE x4, AUTHORITY_CHANGE x1, UNCLASSIFIED x2 -> FULL_REGRESSION_REQUIRED = YES with 25 driver paths (atlas_throughput_001_classifier_audit.json).
targets.instrument: regression_delta classify over the change surface; count of full_regression lane runs in data/regression

targets.population: an ordinary proven data-only market change
targets.current_evidence: Toledo launch 003 ran one broad regression AFTER deploying (toledo_launch, 5714 s) because the deployment record is DEPLOYMENT_CHANGE = mandatory full.

targets.unit: count of broad regressions whose driver set contains no path reachable by the production runtime, the assembler, a shared contract or shared test infrastructure
targets.current_evidence: The classifier decides by PATH PREFIX. All 25 Nashville drivers and 21 Toledo-001 drivers are market-named helpers, discovery configs and proposed/shadow artifacts that no production module imports or reads (atlas_throughput_001_classifier_audit.json; market-local case study in the baseline report).
targets.instrument: regression_delta classify plus an ownership/dependency proof (ATLAS-THROUGHPUT-002)

targets.current_evidence: Gated today by launch_participation_explicit/agrees_with_source (assembler), verify_manifest and verify_authorization (deploy-time); the lineage guard test_deployment_authorization_047::test_the_lineage_is_ordered_and_ends_before_the_current_record (atlas_throughput_001_safety_invariants.md H6).
targets.instrument: the existing gates; a candidate-vs-previous-deploy market-set diff in the release coordinator

targets.current_evidence: Route-level preservation is gated only for the 132 Columbus routes of 2026-08-09 (deploy/netlify/live_production_routes.txt); the other live markets are protected by count gates and hand-recorded live_verification_results (H7).
targets.instrument: previous deploy's sitemap vs candidate sitemap, route set difference == {} (procedural today)

targets.current_evidence: No build-time or deploy-time gate; first-party binding is a write-time rule and a test (H2).

targets.unit: count of TRUE_NEW_FAILURE in the critical safety lane
targets.current_evidence: The 160-node known baseline contains 0 nodes in the IDENTITY/POLICY/ARTIFACT/RELEASE critical groups: 150 ENVIRONMENT (gitignored data/ corpora absent in a fresh worktree) and 10 HISTORICAL_COUNT/PIN (atlas_throughput_001_failure_baseline_audit.json).

targets.unit: count of failures excused without a named class and a named work order
targets.current_evidence: Every failing node in a broad run gets exactly one of PRE_EXISTING / EXPECTED_EPOCH_CHANGE / TEST_HARNESS_FLAKE / TRUE_NEW_FAILURE (regression_lanes.classify); the demo-media module is deselected in the committed baselines but NOT by the lane runner, which is a documented, not silent, difference.
targets.instrument: regression_lanes classify output committed per order
